text: SPOs and CAOs who were found to have done so will be subject to strict disciplinary action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For serious cases, they may be subject to criminal proceedings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if SPF will equip all officers with body-worn cameras to mitigate the risk of wrongful accusations and misuse of powers and if such video footage will be kept safely to prevent cyber attacks and misuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Currently, our frontline Police officers, including SPOs, are equipped with body-worn cameras to facilitate investigations and the gathering of evidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Video footages from these cameras are also useful to address allegations of wrongdoing, such as the recent case where our Police officers were falsely accused of abusing their authority to confront an elderly lady in May 2021, when they actually were telling her domestic helper to remind her to wear a mask and even bought her a packet of food.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For CAOs, we are reviewing the need to equip them with body-worn cameras, similarly, to aid investigations and prevent allegations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: SPF has in place strict protocols governing the use and access to such data.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Typically, SPF only shares data with other Government agencies if provided for under the law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: These security measures help to guard against data breaches and the misuse of data.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We note Mr Melvin Yong’s suggestion for SPF to have a more structured deployment scheme to better leverage the talents of our full-time and operationally-ready NSmen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: When deploying officers to NS vocations, SPF already takes into consideration factors such as the officer’s skills and aptitude.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To better leverage the talents of our NSmen, these officers are provided with multiple pathways within SPF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, officers with background in nautical studies may be deployed to the Police Coast Guard, while officers with expertise in photography may be deployed to the Public Affairs Department to create media content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: When officers transit to become operationally-ready NSmen, they may be provided with the option to change their vocation based on their skill sets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, officers with a background in psychology may serve as counsellors in the Police Psychological Services Department.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We will continuously review the deployment process to further improve the NS experience and to optimise our manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: On empowering the Commissioner to delegate powers to civilian officers in leadership positions, Mr Sharael Taha, Ms Sylvia Lim and Dr Shahira Abdullah asked what type of powers the Commissioner will and will not be able to delegate to civilian officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Sharael Taha also asked about the circumstances under which the Commissioner will delegate such powers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The current intent behind clause 5 of the Bill is to allow the Commissioner to delegate more administrative powers, such as that to issue internal orders to civilian officers in leadership positions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To illustrate, the Director of the Commercial Affairs Department, who is a civilian officer, will be able to directly issue SOPs on managing suspects of commercial and financial crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Currently, he will need to ask a Police officer to do so on his behalf.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Once this provision comes into force, he will no longer need to do so, thus improving operational efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Clause 5 makes explicit that the list of non-delegable powers are those in section 18 and 110A of the PFA, as well as under the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Act (POSSPA).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, this includes the power to give special authorisations to Police officers to impose curfew under POSSPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if SPF intends to allow civilian officers to take over command duties and if civilian officers will have the relevant expertise and credibility to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We would like to clarify that SPF already has civilian officers in leadership positions who assume command duties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, the current Director of the Commercial Affairs Department is a non-Police officer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The benefit of civilianising more leadership posts is that SPF can draw from a wider range of experiences, competencies and perspectives, beyond the pool of uniformed officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We recognise that there are powers which require the specialised knowledge of a Police officer who has had years of experience with policing, such as the power to disperse an unlawful assembly by military force.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: These powers are best exercised by the Commissioner or the Police officers in leadership positions and will remain that way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: This allows the SPF to draw from a wider pool of skillsets, in order to bring perpetrators of such crimes to justice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Many Members raised questions about retaining the employment of regular officers during major crises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked under what circumstances the Commissioner may refuse notices of resignation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Second, when the Minister for Home Affairs has given an activation order under the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Activation orders are only given when a serious incident has occurred, such as a terrorist attack.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Police officers may decide to resign during a crisis for a variety of reasons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In assessing whether to accept or reject a notice of resignation, the Commissioner may take into consideration the reason behind the resignation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, if it is due to the Police officer having a medical condition that does not allow him to serve in SPF, the Commissioner will likely accept this resignation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if Police officers who have indicated their unwillingness to stay in SPF should be retained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: First, I would like to assure the House that our Police officers are extremely dedicated to their duties and I have no doubt that they will rise to the challenge, especially during a crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: While we do not wish to retain anybody who does not want to serve, we also have to balance against the needs of the society during times of emergency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: This is especially important to prevent a scenario where there could be mass resignations that would compromise SPF's operational efficiency in responding to the crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested creating an appeal board to preside over appeals against rejections of notices of resignation and to be redeployed to perform other duties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Given the fast-paced, uncertain and dynamic nature of a crisis, it may not be prudent or even feasible for appeal boards to convene in the thick of the crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But that said, we recognise that there may be Police officers who desire to serve the nation and support the efforts to overcome a crisis in other ways, such as in the healthcare sector instead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The Commissioner may take this into consideration when assessing the notice of resignation, along with other factors, such as SPF’s manpower situation and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Should a Police officer’s notice of resignation be rejected, SPF will internally assess his ability to serve in the roles assigned to him.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: If need be, he may be redeployed in other roles within SPF to more effectively carry out duties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about SPF’s plans to ensure that SPF will be adequately staffed to withstand crises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: During major crises which require more frontline officers, SPF may redeploy more regular Police officers and full-time NSmen from back-end roles to serve at the frontline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: SPF may also recall and mobilise operationally-ready NSmen, Volunteer Ex-NSmen and Volunteer Special Constabulary Officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The wealth of experience these officers have acquired over years of NS and volunteering will help SPF in its efforts to effectively overcome the crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Moving on, I will touch on protecting officers from liability for acts done in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked about the regulations that the Minister for Home Affairs may prescribe in determining what constitutes "good faith and reasonable care".

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Such matters and circumstances may include the operating environment in which the officer is acting, the standards and practices the officer has to follow and the resources to which the officer has access to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: MHA will be prescribing these in subsidiary legislation to allow for greater flexibility to make refinements over time, given our officers’ constantly changing operating environment and standards in response to the ever-evolving security landscape and threats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: More details will be ready in due course, when the subsidiary legislation is formulated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked for examples where officers did not act in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In general, such cases are few and far between.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But that said, I can give two hypothetical examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Another example is if a Police officer fails to respond to and investigate a 999 distress call by an individual known to SPF as being the target of repeated physical domestic violence and the individual dies from injuries from the abuser.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I want to emphasise that the protection that we will be according to officers is not unconditional and is subject to them acting in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Making explicit this protection in law will allow our officers to more effectively carry out their duties, such as preventing crime or saving lives, without the distractions and the constant concerns about getting sued or being held liable for injuries or damage to property.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To address Mr Desmond Choo’s question on whether superiors will be held liable if their subordinates did not act in good faith and with reasonable care, this will very much depend on the facts and circumstances of the case, such as whether the superior had knowledge or control over his subordinate’s actions at that point in time or could reasonably be expected to be able to stop or influence his actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked if this protection will be extended to Prison officers and other Home Team officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To clarify, many of our Home Team officers already have protections from liability under other legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, SCDF officers are protected from liability for acts done in good faith and with reasonable care in the execution of the Civil Defence Act and the Fire Safety Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For Prison officers, they are currently not explicitly protected in legislation although they are already covered under the common law defence of necessity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: MHA will likewise consider making explicit this protection for Prison officers and other Home Team officers in their relevant legislation where opportune, just as we have done so in the PFA for Police officers and the Civil Defence Act for SCDF officers in 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Next, Dr Shahira Abdullah had suggested that persons who manufacture Police uniforms or insignia should seek the Commissioner’s written permission.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To clarify, SPF already has in place a transparent framework to regulate the market for Police uniforms or insignia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: None of these permissions are given verbally and all are written in black and white.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For example, persons who wish to manufacture Police uniforms are required to bid for an open tender.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Those who are successful are subject to conditions in the contract, which include the specifications of the uniforms they are allowed to manufacture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Next, Mr Desmond Choo asked about legal liabilities for Auxiliary Police Force (APF) employers that infringe sections 87(5), (7) and (8) in clause 21 of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The existing section 90 already allows the Commissioner to take certain actions if an APF employer infringes any provision in Part IX of the Police Force Act (PFA), which includes clause 21 of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: These actions include suspending or revoking the authorisation for the creation of an APF as well as the imposition of financial penalties on the APF employer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked if section 88 in clause 22 of the Bill applies to entities and persons with indirect control over the board of the APF employer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I stated earlier that clause 22 will require a person to seek the Minister's approval before becoming an indirect controller as defined in clause 17 of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo cited the example of a company with a controlling stake in the parent company owning the APF employer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: If such control involves the holding of equity interest or control of voting power in the APF employer, then, depending on the facts, this may fall under the definition of a 5%, 25%, 50% or 75% controller in clause 17.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I would also like to assure Mr Raj Joshua Thomas that SPF will continue to work closely with the APFs to prevent any infringement of the PFA and Private Security Industry Act (PSIA) in advertising their armed and unarmed services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: That the vast majority of residents in Singapore feel assured that they can walk home safe at night is not a matter of chance or coincidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: It is a result of decades of effective policing, supported by robust laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Let us continue to keep Singapore safe and secure.
